## Tooling situation

I have no ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed, or web-access tool in this session, and no network access — so I could not run a live registry query. Everything below is from my own knowledge (training cutoff May 2026). **Recruitment status is the one thing that changes fastest, so treat the "active" labels as "was active as of my cutoff" and verify before relying on them.**

The query that answers this definitively:

```
https://clinicaltrials.gov/search?term=KRAS%20G12C&aggFilters=status:rec%20act
```
or via the API:
```
https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.term=KRAS+G12C&filter.overallStatus=RECRUITING|ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING
```

## Yes — the space is large and active

As of early-to-mid 2026 there were on the order of **100+ registered trials** involving KRAS G12C inhibitors, with a dozen or more in Phase 3. Two agents are FDA-approved (so trials are now mostly combination, earlier-line, and head-to-head), and three more are approved in China.

### Approved agents and their pivotal/ongoing programs

**Sotorasib (AMG 510, Lumakras/Lumykras — Amgen)** — FDA accelerated approval May 2021 (2L+ NSCLC); Jan 2025 with panitumumab for KRAS G12C mCRC.
- CodeBreaK 100 — Phase 1/2, NSCLC + other solid tumors — **NCT03600883**
- CodeBreaK 200 — Phase 3 vs docetaxel, 2L NSCLC (met PFS endpoint) — **NCT04303780**
- CodeBreaK 300 — Phase 3 + panitumumab, chemorefractory mCRC — **NCT05198934**
- CodeBreaK 101 — Phase 1b combination master protocol (panitumumab, pembrolizumab, trametinib, afatinib, carboplatin/pemetrexed…) — **NCT04185883**
- CodeBreaK 201 — Phase 2, pancreatic and other non-lung/non-CRC solid tumors
- Also: 1L NSCLC chemo-combination and 1L mCRC (+FOLFIRI) Phase 3s. *NCT IDs for these last two I do not recall reliably — look them up.*

**Adagrasib (MRTX849, Krazati — Mirati/Bristol Myers Squibb)** — FDA accelerated approval Dec 2022 (NSCLC); June 2024 with cetuximab (mCRC).
- KRYSTAL-1 — Phase 1/2, multi-tumor — **NCT03785249**
- KRYSTAL-7 — Phase 2/3 + pembrolizumab, 1L NSCLC — **NCT04613596**
- KRYSTAL-12 — Phase 3 vs docetaxel, 2L NSCLC (met PFS endpoint) — **NCT04685135**
- KRYSTAL-10 — Phase 3 + cetuximab vs chemo, 2L mCRC — **NCT04793958**
- Plus KRYSTAL-2/-14/-16/-17 combination studies, and a notable CNS-metastasis cohort (adagrasib has meaningful CSF penetration).

**China-approved G12C inhibitors** (each with ongoing registrational and combination work):
- **Fulzerasib** (GFH925 / IBI351, Innovent/GenFleet) — NMPA approval 2024, NSCLC
- **Glecirasib** (JAB-21822, Jacobio) — NMPA approval 2025, NSCLC
- **Garsorasib** (D-1553, InventisBio) — NSCLC and CRC programs

### Next-generation / investigational agents in active development

| Agent | Sponsor | Notable trials |
|---|---|---|
| **Divarasib** (GDC-6036) | Genentech/Roche | Phase 1/1b **NCT04449874** (ORR ~53–56% in NSCLC — best-in-class signal); Phase 3 "KRASCENDO" program in NSCLC and CRC |
| **Olomorasib** (LY3537982) | Eli Lilly | Phase 1/2 **NCT04956640**; SUNRAY-01 Phase 3 + pembrolizumab, 1L NSCLC (**NCT06119581**, verify) |
| **Elironrasib** (RMC-6291) | Revolution Medicines | Phase 1 **NCT05462717**; combos with daraxonrasib (RMC-6236, pan-RAS) |
| **MK-1084** | Merck | Phase 1/2 **NCT05067283**; Phase 3 + pembrolizumab, 1L NSCLC |
| **Opnurasib** (JDQ443) | Novartis | KontRASt-01 / KontRASt-02 Phase 3 (**NCT05132075**, verify) — program was deprioritized |
| **BI 1823911** | Boehringer Ingelheim | Phase 1, incl. combination with SOS1 inhibitor BI 1701963 |
| **D3S-001** | D3 Bio | Phase 1/2 |

Discontinued, for completeness: JNJ-74699157 (ARS-3248), and several early Chinese candidates.

### Caveats on my confidence

- Drug names, sponsors, trial names, approval milestones, and phase/indication: **high confidence**.
- Specific NCT numbers: **moderate confidence** — the CodeBreaK 100/200 and KRYSTAL-1/-7 IDs I am most sure of; the Phase 3s for divarasib, olomorasib, MK-1084 and the newer CodeBreaK studies I would verify before citing in writing.
- Current recruiting-vs-closed status for any individual trial: **not verifiable here.**

## ANSWER

Yes — many. KRAS G12C is one of the most crowded targets in oncology, with 100+ registered trials and a dozen-plus Phase 3s as of my May 2026 knowledge cutoff. Two inhibitors are FDA-approved (sotorasib/Lumakras, adagrasib/Krazati) and three more approved in China (fulzerasib, glecirasib, garsorasib); next-generation agents divarasib, olomorasib, elironrasib, MK-1084 and others are in active Phase 1–3 development. Key trials: CodeBreaK 100/200/300 (NCT03600883, NCT04303780, NCT05198934), KRYSTAL-1/7/12/10 (NCT03785249, NCT04613596, NCT04685135, NCT04793958), divarasib NCT04449874, olomorasib NCT04956640.

This is recalled knowledge, not a live registry lookup — I have no ClinicalTrials.gov or web tool in this session. Confirm current status at `clinicaltrials.gov/search?term=KRAS G12C&aggFilters=status:rec act`.
